intro: North Saanich has acreages, hobby farms and waterfront homes from Deep Cove to Lands End, along with townhouse stratas near Dean Park.

The Tree Protection Bylaw requires a permit to remove regulated trees, which can be smaller in environmental and steep-slope areas. Topping is prohibited. Permits are reviewed by staff and must be posted before work, so plan ahead. See [tree and vegetation work](/services/tree-vegetation/) or [request a free quote](/quote/).
See [sample projects](/portfolio/) and our [seasonal guides](/resources/) for more.

localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

North Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1548 requires a permit to remove any regulated tree (generally 20 cm diameter or more, smaller for arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific dogwood, yew and shore pine, plus trees in environmental or steep-slope areas). Topping is prohibited; best-practice pruning needs no permit. Staff review takes about 2-3 weeks and the permit must be posted 48 hours before work.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.
